question: Let $A=[a_{ij}]$ and $B=[b_{ij}]$ be matrices of order $3\times3$ whose elements are defined by $a_{ij}=2i-j$ and $b_{ij}=i+j$, where $1\leq i,j\leq3$. Construct the matrices $A$ and $B$ and hence determine the matrix $2A-B$ together with its order.
explanation:
Formation of the Matrices

For $A=[a_{ij}]$, the elements are given by $a_{ij}=2i-j$. Substituting $i,j=1,2,3$, we obtain $a_{11}=1$, $a_{12}=0$, $a_{13}=-1$, $a_{21}=3$, $a_{22}=2$, $a_{23}=1$, $a_{31}=5$, $a_{32}=4$ and $a_{33}=3$. Hence, $$A=\begin{bmatrix}1&0&-1\\3&2&1\\5&4&3\end{bmatrix}$$ Similarly, for $B=[b_{ij}]$, $b_{ij}=i+j$. Therefore, $$B=\begin{bmatrix}2&3&4\\3&4&5\\4&5&6\end{bmatrix}$$

Evaluation

Multiplying each element of $A$ by $2$, $$2A=\begin{bmatrix}2&0&-2\\6&4&2\\10&8&6\end{bmatrix}$$ Therefore, $$2A-B=\begin{bmatrix}2&0&-2\\6&4&2\\10&8&6\end{bmatrix}-\begin{bmatrix}2&3&4\\3&4&5\\4&5&6\end{bmatrix}$$ $$2A-B=\begin{bmatrix}0&-3&-6\\3&0&-3\\6&3&0\end{bmatrix}$$ Since the resulting matrix contains three rows and three columns, its order is $3\times3$. Thus, the required matrix is $\begin{bmatrix}0&-3&-6\\3&0&-3\\6&3&0\end{bmatrix}$ of order $3\times3$.
